name: Norval Foundation
funding: Property investor Louis Norval financed it entirely at the 2018 opening and set up a capital fund. Sponsors include Schroders (art prize), Stonehage Fleming (2021 auction) and Sanlam.

name: Zeitz MOCAA
funding: Jochen Zeitz donated the collection he had loaned; sponsors include Gucci and BMW, the Mellon Foundation funds fellowships, and the board now pays.

name: Bag Factory Artists' Studios
funding: National Arts Council South Africa, Triangle Network, international cultural foundations, studio rentals. Registered Non-Profit Organisation (NPO).

name: Origins Centre
funding: Wits campus museum, opened 2006; its Rock Art Research Institute is funded by the National Research Foundation, Wits' research fund and Anglo American's Chairman's Fund. No centre funder list.

name: Wits Art Museum
funding: University of the Witwatersrand museum. Standard Bank has been collection partner since 1978 and 1979; early donors include Norman Herber, Jack Ginsberg, John Schlesinger and Gertrude Posel.

name: National Arts Festival
funding: Eastern Cape government, Sarah Baartman District Municipality, National Lottery Commission, Standard Bank. National government gave R5.5 million for 2022 to 2024, nothing in 2025, a smaller grant in 2026.

name: Javett Art Centre at the University of Pretoria (Javett-UP)
funding: University of Pretoria gave the land and funding. The Javett Foundation funded construction and pledged ten years of annual gifts for running costs and an endowment.

name: Busan Biennale
funding: 2026 edition run by the Busan Biennale Organizing Committee for Busan Metropolitan City, with BNK Busan Bank, Shinsegae, Naver and Danish, Dutch and UK cultural funds.

name: Busan Museum of Art
funding: Municipal museum run by Busan Metropolitan City, reopened in 2026 after a 46.9bn-won rebuild; patrons' society members include BNK Busan Bank and Hwaseung Group.

name: Busan Museum of Contemporary Art
funding: Municipal museum on Eulsukdo, run by Busan Metropolitan City; it hosted part of the 2026 Busan Biennale.
